messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 bar), water’s freezing point is lowered relative to the standard 0 °C at 101.3 kPa.  
Using the water phase diagram (or the Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid transition), the freezing point at 10 kPa is about **–2 °C** (≈ –1.9 °C).  

So, under a pressure of 10 kPa, pure water will freeze at roughly –2 °C.
